classification.difficultyReason: Express both the target angle and the sum of the two labelled angles as supplementary to angle A, then equate them.

content.prompt: Consider the cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ shown below. Prove that $\angle 1=\angle 2+\angle 3$.

spec.description: Cyclic quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal BD and three labelled angle sectors. Decorative purple sector fills are replaced by unfilled angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: Angle 1 is BCD; angle 2 is ADB; angle 3 is ABD.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and angle labels are visible.

answer.worked:
In $\triangle ABD$, the interior angles sum to $180^\circ$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle A&=180^\circ-(\angle 2+\angle 3).\end{align*}$$
Opposite angles of the cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary:
$$\begin{align*}\angle A&=180^\circ-\angle 1.\end{align*}$$
Equating these expressions gives
$$\begin{align*}180^\circ-(\angle 2+\angle 3)&=180^\circ-\angle 1,\\\angle 1&=\angle 2+\angle 3.\end{align*}$$
